whyV1IsVoid.summary: v1's run cleared all five bars and the result is DISCARDED, because the baseline it beat was defective.
whyV1IsVoid.defect: positionGroup() misclassified the corpus. ESPN reports a substitute's position as the literal string "SUB" — 13,486 of 30,377 rows — and the old test `p.includes("B")` matched it, so every substitute in the league was classified a DEFENDER. Separately "CD-L"/"CD-R" (centre-backs) and "CF-L"/"CF-R" (centre-forwards) both fell through to UNK, blending the lowest- and highest-scoring outfield positions into one prior across 15.6% of rows.
whyV1IsVoid.whyItMatters: The positional baseline IS bar P1. A baseline that cannot tell a centre-forward from a centre-back is not 'the league base rate for position group x participation state' — it is a weaker thing wearing that name, and beating it proves less than the bar intended. The defect flattered the model, which is the direction that should always void a result rather than excuse it.
whyV1IsVoid.afterTheFix: F 0.2894 goals per appearance, M 0.1223, SUB 0.0450, D 0.0398, G 0.0000, UNK down to 0.62% of rows. Forwards score roughly seven times as often as defenders, and keepers never score — separations the old buckets destroyed.
whyV1IsVoid.contamination: The 2025-26 holdout was scored once under v1 and is therefore BURNED. It is excluded from this protocol entirely rather than reused, because a holdout looked at once is no longer a holdout.

target.definition: did this player score one or more goals in this match
target.why: Unchanged from v1. One market, one bar, no shopping across targets until one passes.

population.rule: every player who APPEARED in a scored match — started or came off the bench
population.honestLimitation: Conditioning on appearance means these numbers do NOT answer 'will he play'. Where no lineup is available at publication time the model must abstain rather than assume a starter.

corpus.source: ESPN public endpoints, free and unmetered
corpus.note: No MINUTES field exists in this source — only started / subbedIn / subbedOut. Participation therefore enters as a discrete state rather than an expected-minutes term. Recorded as a limitation, not solved.

protocol.walkForward: by match date; rates for a match are fitted STRICTLY on matches dated earlier. No same-day information is used.

warmup.rule: folds into the rates, NEVER scored

development.use: ALL hyperparameter search happens here and nowhere else

holdout.use: scored ONCE, after the configuration is locked. This season has NEVER been scored — under v1 it served only as warm-up — which is what makes it a valid holdout after v1 burned 2025-26.

excluded.why: scored under v1; contaminated and deliberately not reused

model.lambda: the player's goals per appearance in his participation state, shrunk toward the positional rate for that same state
model.shrinkage: Bayesian pseudo-count k toward the positional base rate

baselines.definition: the league base rate for (position group x participation state), on the CORRECTED buckets, fitted on prior matches only
baselines.why: The bar that matters. If player history does not beat a correct positional average, the model knows nothing about individual players.

baselines.definition: the player's unshrunk historical rate, positional as fallback when he has no prior appearances
baselines.why: So shrinkage must earn its place rather than be adopted on faith.

primaryMetric: log loss on the binary outcome

acceptanceBars.note: UNCHANGED FROM v1, deliberately. The bars were written before any number was seen and are not renegotiated because a run failed or a defect was found — only the defective baseline is repaired and the contaminated season dropped.

bars.statement: model HOLDOUT log loss must be lower than the corrected positional baseline's by at least 0.005
model HOLDOUT log loss must be lower than or equal to the raw-player baseline's
model HOLDOUT expected calibration error must be at most 0.020
summed predicted probabilities must land within 10% of the observed number of goalscorers
the model must produce a probability for at least 95% of the appeared population

stoppingRule.statement: ONE sweep over the declared grid, on DEVELOPMENT only. If no configuration clears all five bars, the EPL player model is REJECTED and nothing player-level is published. A THIRD attempt is not permitted on this corpus — a second repair would stop being a fix and start being a search.

whatPassingDoesNotMean: It does not mean the model beats a sportsbook price. Odds are not an input.
It does not license shots, shots-on-target, assists or cards — each needs its own bar.
It does not answer whether a player will play.
